_meta.project: instex Spectrograph Explorer presets -- round 7: OHP 1.93 m / ELODIE (fiber-fed white-pupil echelle, prism + grism cross-disperser)
_meta.companion: data/round7/elodie.md (same content as Markdown); structure as data/round6/m2fs_ifum.json
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc, and a short quote. tag: SOURCED / DERIVED / MEASURED / INFERRED / EFFECTIVE / SCHEMATIC / NOT FOUND. derived = arithmetic done here from sourced values (is_derived = the value itself is derived). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). The primary paper (B96) is a scan without a text layer: its quotes are transcribed from the scan and checked against a Tesseract OCR; page numbers are journal pages.
_meta.quote_normalization: NFKC; case-folded; whitespace collapsed (and again with whitespace and hyphens removed); curly quotes, primes, dashes, minus, micro, multiplication, degree and plus-minus signs normalized; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces.
_meta.on_off_axis_verdict: OFF-AXIS (Czerny-Turner mirrors M1/M2 separate; fiber head not in the returning beam); colTilt must not be 0

B96.cite: Baranne, A., Queloz, D., Mayor, M., Adrianzyk, G., Knispel, G., Kohler, D., Lacroix, D., Meunier, J.-P., Rimbaud, G. & Vin, A. 1996, A&AS 119, 373, "ELODIE: A spectrograph for accurate radial velocity measurements" (ADS scan, 18 pp. = journal pp. 373-390; PDF page n = journal page 372 + n). The PDF is a scan WITHOUT a text layer: every quote from it is transcribed from the scan and was machine-checked against a Tesseract 5 OCR of the 300 dpi page images (rawdata/presets/elodie/Baranne1996_tesseract_OCR_derived.txt, a derived file); the figures were read by eye from the same images. OCR noise is kept in quotes where the check needs it (e.g. 'ym' for the micro sign, 'zm', '8°63' printed for 8.63 deg).

echelle_G_eff.quote: The echelle-grating used has a tan ... 102 mm with 31
quote_pieces: The echelle-grating used has a tan
102 mm with 31
echelle_G_eff.derived: G = 2 sin(delta) / (m lambda) with m lambda = 61.0572 um: delta = 75.964 deg -> d = 61.0572/(2 x 0.97014) = 31.468 um -> 31.78 /mm; delta = 75 deg -> 31.64 /mm (the standard R4 ruling is 31.6 /mm; not sourced for ELODIE). With the printed G = 31 /mm and delta = 75.96 deg, 2 d sin(delta) = 62.59 um, 2.5% ABOVE the m lambda of Fig. 3, which needs cos(gamma) = 0.9755, gamma = 12.7 deg: far too large for the layout.
echelle_G_eff.name: Echelle groove density needed to reproduce Fig. 3's order numbers (gamma = 0)
echelle_G_eff.note: CONFLICT (printed 31 /mm vs Fig. 3's order numbers). Most likely '31' is a truncation of 31.6 (INFERRED; the Fig. 1 label theta = 75 deg and 31.64 /mm then agree with the order numbers at gamma = 0 to 0.1%). Predicted linear dispersion at 4964 A with f = 300 mm: lambda/(2 f tan delta) = 2.217 A/mm (delta = 75 deg) or 2.068 A/mm (75.96 deg); Fig. 3 gives 2.133 A/mm, between the two. Recommendation: G = 31.78 /mm at delta = 75.96 deg (EFFECTIVE; keeps tan theta = 4) or 31.64 at 75; both keep m lambda; flag as EFFECTIVE in the preset.

layout_levels.value: two levels (Fig. 1). LEVEL 1 (Czerny-Turner, in the horizontal plane of the bench): fibers -> M1 (toroidal, f/15, at the far end of the bench, bottom of the mirror plate) -> echelle (Littrow, conic: slightly out of plane) -> M2 (middle of the plate) -> intermediate spectrum (telecentric, in a plane 'symmetrical to the source with respect to the grating', i.e. beside the echelle) -> small flat mirror next to the echelle -> M3 (top of the plate, concave, 'a new collimator') -> white pupil of 75 mm. LEVEL 2: M3 beam -> prism F2 -> grism -> camera F3 (lens, f/3), pointing up from the plane of level 1 (the camera is drawn above and beyond the echelle)
layout_levels.quote: the echelle grat ... ing is put at the common focus of both adjacent mirrors ... M1 and M2 ... A small mirror near the intermediate spectrum sends back the monochromatic beams towards a third concave mirror M3 ... This third mirror is a new collimator for all these beams which

layout_levels.name: Optical layout: element order
layout_levels.note: 'common focus of both adjacent mirrors' is the text's description of the echelle's place; with the stated f/15 collimator and a collimated beam between M1 and the echelle, the echelle stands about one collimator focal length from the mirrors (see layout_distance); the wording is ambiguous and is not used for a number. Folds: the small flat near the echelle (angle NOT FOUND, SCHEMATIC) and the 'removal mirror and beam splitting' of the accelerometry experiment in the front end (irrelevant to the spectrograph).

layout_sides.value: Viewed from the fiber side: the fibers and the echelle are at the near end; the mirror plate (M1 bottom round, M2 middle, M3 top, both rectangular) stands at the far end of the bench; the small flat (a thin rectangular plate) is fixed on top of the echelle's right end; the prism F2 + grism + camera are above and to the left of the echelle, looking back toward the plate; the camera axis points up-left
layout_sides.name: Which side each element sits (Fig. 1 / OHPF layout.gif, perspective, read from the figure)
layout_sides.note: Read by eye from a perspective drawing. Left/right of the drawing is not a physical left/right.

layout_distance.value: NOT PUBLISHED. MEASURED lower bound from Fig. 1: the 408 mm echelle spans 204 px of the 1400-px-wide render of the figure (2.0 mm/px); the echelle center to the center of M2 is 628 px, so >= 1256 mm along the (foreshortened) bench axis; consistent with f_col = 1530 mm
layout_distance.derived: 408 mm / 204 px = 2.0 mm/px along the echelle's long edge; 628 px x 2.0 mm/px = 1256 mm (a perspective view at an oblique angle: the true distance is longer). Method: pixel counts on the 300 dpi scan scaled to 1400 px width.
